senses.definition: a state of temporary disuse or suspension
senses.example: The plans were held in abeyance until funding was found.

senses.definition: growth or increase by the gradual accumulation of additional layers or matter
senses.example: The island formed by the accretion of coral over millennia.

senses.definition: the highest point in the development of something; a climax or culmination
senses.example: The empire reached its apogee under the third king.

senses.definition: a flattering or pleasing statement or action used to persuade someone gently to do something
senses.example: Despite all their blandishments, she refused to sell her land.

senses.definition: hypocritical and sanctimonious talk, typically of a moral, religious or political nature
senses.example: He was tired of the cant about family values.

senses.definition: the jargon of a particular group
senses.example: The memo was written in management cant.

senses.definition: swiftness of movement
senses.example: The fire crew responded with celerity.

senses.definition: showing a high degree of skill and flair; complete or perfect
senses.example: She was a consummate professional who never missed a deadline.

senses.definition: to make a marriage or relationship complete
senses.example: The deal was consummated with a handshake.

senses.definition: a small group of people with shared interests or tastes, especially one that is exclusive of other people
senses.example: A coterie of loyal fans followed the band from city to city.

senses.definition: greed for money or possessions
senses.example: The cupidity of the landlord was well known.

senses.definition: having or showing refined taste or good judgment
senses.example: The shop caters to discriminating collectors.

words.note: As a compliment, discriminating means having refined taste.

senses.definition: feeling or expressing great sorrow or distress
senses.example: The violin played a dolorous melody.

senses.definition: to restrict or burden someone or something in such a way that free action or movement is difficult
senses.example: She was encumbered with heavy bags.

senses.definition: to deliberately avoid using; to abstain from
senses.example: The chef eschews frozen food.

senses.definition: (of a plant) pale and drawn out due to a lack of light
senses.example: The etiolated seedlings had grown in a dark shed.

senses.definition: having lost vigor or substance; feeble
senses.example: The book is an etiolated version of a great story.

senses.definition: to reveal the presence of a quality or feeling
senses.example: The students evinced little interest in the topic.

senses.definition: to search out and destroy completely
senses.example: The government vowed to extirpate corruption.

senses.definition: relating or inclined to dissension
senses.example: The factious council could not agree on a budget.

words.note: Factious means divided into quarreling factions; fractious means unruly or irritable.

senses.definition: to restrict the freedom of
senses.example: She felt fettered by the rules of the old firm.

senses.definition: a chain or manacle used to restrain a prisoner, or a restraint in general
senses.example: The prisoners' fetters clanked as they walked.

senses.definition: (of an organization or system) new or inexperienced
senses.example: The fledgling company had only three employees.

senses.definition: a young bird that has just grown the feathers it needs to fly
senses.example: The fledgling hopped along the branch.

senses.definition: complimentary or flattering to an excessive degree
senses.example: The fulsome praise of the new boss embarrassed even him.

words.note: Fulsome often implies excessive or insincere praise, not just generous praise.

senses.definition: devoid of guile; innocent and without deception
senses.example: Her guileless face made it easy to trust her.

senses.definition: just begun and so not fully formed or developed; rudimentary
senses.example: Her ideas for the book were still inchoate.

senses.definition: to instill an attitude, idea or habit by persistent instruction
senses.example: The school tries to inculcate a love of learning.

senses.definition: poor; needy
senses.example: The clinic offers free care to indigent patients.

senses.definition: naive, simplistic and superficial
senses.example: The article's jejune analysis ignored the real causes.

senses.definition: (of ideas or writing) dull; uninspiring
senses.example: The jejune lecture put half the room to sleep.

senses.definition: generosity in bestowing money or gifts upon others
senses.example: The museum was built thanks to the largesse of a local family.

senses.definition: to exaggerate or feign illness in order to escape duty or work
senses.example: The manager suspected she was malingering to avoid the audit.

senses.definition: lacking imagination, foresight or intellectual insight
senses.example: The myopic policy ignored the long-term costs.

senses.definition: nearsighted
senses.example: Myopic children may struggle to read the board.

senses.definition: the lowest point in the fortunes of a person or organization
senses.example: The team reached its nadir with ten straight losses.

senses.definition: to irritate or annoy someone
senses.example: Her condescending tone nettled him.

senses.definition: harsh criticism or censure
senses.example: The decision drew international opprobrium.

senses.definition: showing excessive confidence or pride
senses.example: His overweening ambition alienated his allies.

senses.definition: a small, relatively unimportant offense or sin
senses.example: The press seized on his youthful peccadilloes.

senses.definition: a bitter attack or denunciation, especially a verbal one
senses.example: The senator's philippic against the bill lasted an hour.

senses.definition: a person who is hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts
senses.example: Only a philistine would pave over the old gardens.

senses.definition: done, made or acting suddenly or without careful consideration
senses.example: Their precipitate decision to sell the house was soon regretted.

senses.definition: to cause an event or situation, typically one that is bad or undesirable, to happen suddenly or prematurely
senses.example: The assassination precipitated a war.

words.note: Precipitate means rash or hasty; precipitous means steep or sudden.

senses.definition: the state of being close to someone or something; proximity
senses.example: Friendships often form through simple propinquity.

senses.definition: close kinship
senses.example: The propinquity of the two families made the marriage awkward.

senses.definition: making or indicating timely preparation for the future
senses.example: A provident farmer stores grain for lean years.

senses.definition: showing great attention to detail or correct behavior
senses.example: He was punctilious about answering every letter within a day.

senses.definition: strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something
senses.example: The village is redolent of an earlier, slower age.

senses.definition: strongly smelling of something
senses.example: The kitchen was redolent of garlic and thyme.

senses.definition: health-giving; healthy
senses.example: The mountain air was thought to be salubrious.

senses.definition: (of a place) pleasant; not run-down
senses.example: They moved to a more salubrious part of town.

senses.definition: conduct or speech inciting people to rebel against the authority of a state or monarch
senses.example: The journalist was jailed for sedition.

senses.definition: to quench or satisfy one's thirst
senses.example: We slaked our thirst at a mountain stream.

senses.definition: a grammatical mistake in speech or writing
senses.example: The essay was marred by solecisms.

senses.definition: a breach of good manners; a piece of incorrect behavior
senses.example: Arriving without a gift was a social solecism.

senses.definition: (of a person's voice) loud and powerful
senses.example: The sergeant's stentorian voice carried across the parade ground.

senses.definition: (of a person) lying face upward
senses.example: The patient lay supine on the table.

senses.definition: failing to act or protest as a result of moral weakness or indolence
senses.example: The supine board did nothing to stop the fraud.

senses.definition: to offer or present something formally
senses.example: The minister tendered her resignation.

senses.definition: showing gentleness and concern or sympathy
senses.example: He gave her a tender look.

words.note: As a verb, tender means to offer formally.

senses.definition: a person who behaves obsequiously to someone important
senses.example: The director was surrounded by toadies.

senses.definition: to act in an obsequious way
senses.example: She refused to toady to the new owners.

senses.definition: not permanent
senses.example: Their happiness was transitory.

senses.definition: depraved or wicked behavior or character
senses.example: He was dismissed for moral turpitude.
